description:
The I-5 corridor in California as eleven named stretches (strips) on the I-5 centerline, from San Ysidro (s = 0 m) to the Oregon line (s ≈ 1,281,400 m), and the dog stops in any stretch, mile range or window ahead of a point. Every stop carries its s in meters from San Ysidro, its Caltrans odometer mile, the side of the road it serves (right or left of northbound travel, or both), its distance off the freeway, the road's elevation, and restrooms, water, pet area, dog park and hours as its official source states them. A family stop is one whose official source states restrooms and a pet area or dog park. A paired stop is a freeway exit with places to stop for people nearby (located through OpenStreetMap, counted by kind, never named and not verified for restrooms) matched to the nearest DogPolicies place that allows dogs within about a mile, with its rule and source.

With no stretch, miles or point, the result is the list of stretches with their s and mile ranges and stop counts. Strips: sandiego (San Ysidro → Camp Pendleton), orange-la (Camp Pendleton → East LA), grapevine (East LA → Wheeler Ridge), kern-westside (Wheeler Ridge → Kettleman), westside (Kettleman → Santa Nella), delta (Santa Nella → Stockton), sacramento (Stockton → Woodland), valley (Woodland → Williams), tehama (Williams → Red Bluff), shasta (Red Bluff → Mt Shasta), siskiyou (Mt Shasta → Siskiyou Summit).

Examples:
  - "What is between the Grapevine and Kettleman?" -> strip="grapevine" (East LA to Wheeler Ridge) and strip="kern-westside" (Wheeler Ridge to Kettleman)
  - "The next 5 family stops northbound from Stockton" -> near={lat:37.95, lon:-121.29}, direction="north", family=true, limit=5
  - "Every stop between mile 300 and 340" -> from_mile=300, to_mile=340
  - "Exits with somewhere for people and a park for the dog in the Sacramento stretch" -> strip="sacramento", paired=true

ahead_miles.description: Window in miles from near in the direction of travel

direction.description: Direction of travel from near; north means increasing s

dog_friendly_only.description: Leave out stops where dogs are not allowed

from_mile.description: Start of a mile range (Caltrans odometer)

kinds.description: Kinds of stops to include; all by default

near.description: A point on or near I-5; the window starts at the nearest point of the road

paired.description: Also list the paired stops in the window

response_format.description: 'markdown' for readable text, 'json' for structured data

strip.description: A stretch by id (sandiego, orange-la, grapevine, kern-westside, westside, delta, sacramento, valley, tehama, shasta, siskiyou)

name: dogpolicies_i5_corridor

code.description: With an outcome other than ok: not_found, invalid, unavailable

did_you_mean.description: Close matches to what was asked for: towns, places, slugs or brands, best first

nearest.description: When nothing is inside the radius: the nearest places in the data, with distance_miles

nearest_i5.description: With a point too far from I-5: the nearest point on I-5 and how far it is

next.description: Calls that would answer the question, in words

outcome.description: Absent or ok: a normal answer. no_match: nothing in the data matches, see did_you_mean, nearest and next. bad_input: the arguments cannot be used as given, see next. partial: some of the ids were found, see missing. unavailable: a live source could not be read. None of these is an error.

citation.description: Copy-ready citation: answer, source, date checked, record URL, license

confidence.description: stated: the place's own source says it; inferred_from_agency: an agency-wide rule; inherited_brand: the chain's policy, not confirmed by this hotel

freshness.description: fresh: inside its review interval; due: past it; stale: past twice it, confirm before you go; unreadable: the last check could not read the source

uid.description: Stable id that survives a rename

title: I-5 corridor by stretch
